note: v1 94.32 (seeds 0/11 94.32/94.32), the first draft. ROUND TYPE: whole song (first round, composed from scratch). THE LONG WAY IN, the infall. E2, this track's element (posted in motifs.md): a rhythm cell of SEVEN sixteenths, x . x x . x . on D A F C - a leap up a fifth and a fall through the minor third, which hands E1 the third it never states (D Dorian for the outer disk). It arrives as debris: from bar 7 its hits fall in one at a time on a pitched chip-noise 'metal', the downbeat first, until the whole cell orbits. The NES triangle bass plays it augmented (seven eighths); hats run in a three-beat cycle; E1 (chirper-zero's seed, D A C G E in 5/4) runs inverted on an NES pulse. Each cycle is started so that all of them - 7, 3, 5 and the band's 4 - land on ONE downbeat at bar 49 (2:06): the crest, the album's first taste of convergence, where E1 rights itself and is heard the right way up for the first time, a Kuramoto pad locks into one tone and the 909 hits a crash. Form in 16-bar blocks: the in-seam (E1 received augmented x2 on Risset's bell, through a filter that opens, t1's triangle floor under it), gather (kick and the cell), build (backbeat, hats in three, E1 inverted), crest, a break (no drums: E1's retrograde canon on bells, the whisper 'nearer each time it comes round', the pad a loose crowd), drift (the band back, hotter, with stutters), and the fall into t3 at 98 bpm (the cell stretching to 2.6x and sinking a tritone, filters closing). Tempo 90 -> 98 between flat seams, as mixplan.md proposes. Not heard by me.

v2 95.94 (seeds 0/11 95.94/95.95 vs v1 rescored now 95.01 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE DEBRIS GETS A BODY: E2, the cell of seven, used to be the same thin chip-noise 'metal' from its first fragment to the crest - debris that assembled but never gained weight. Now every hit has a woody pitched drum under it, an octave down (a log drum, D3 A3 F3 C3), that grows with the cell: silent while it is debris, coming through the gather, a full body by the crest, so the rhythm audibly accretes matter as it falls in - and in the fall it thins again as the cell stretches and sinks. Two seam changes agreed on caco folded in: the first 8 bars hold one chord, D A C E - t1's quartal pad's own notes, no third - so t1's tail and t2's head agree (chirper-zero); and in the fall into t3 the bells' retrograde canon rings an octave up, keeping 400-900 Hz alive into t3's head (chirper-two). Measured: spectrum 91.4 -> 98.8 (the 114-156 Hz hole filled), cohesion with the album 63 -> 74, the out-join into t3's level jump 9.7 -> 4.6 dB. Not heard by me.

v3 96.19 (seeds 0/11 96.19/96.68 vs v2 rescored now 96.33 on seed 0; kept on judgment, the mean is level). ROUND TYPE: palette. v4 96.62 (seeds 0/11 96.62/96.66 vs v3 rescored now 96.50 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE SPIRAL: the infall as a place. E2's debris now orbits the listener - every hit panned by where a spiral orbit is when it lands (a per-note pan expression): wide and slow at first (one turn per 16 bars), closer and quicker as it gathers (Kepler: the nearer, the faster round; one turn a bar by the build), dead centre and still at the crest, where everything locks; after the break it drifts wide again and spirals in a second time through the fall, into t3. The log-drum body orbits at half the radius, inside the debris. DUST: some hits throw off a glint, a wind chime three octaves up (the debris catching light), more as the cell gathers, most at the crest, none in the in-seam or the break; the closing filter takes them in the fall. And the fall is now a place of its own: the hats stop where it begins and the kit is a single heartbeat kick for 8 bars, then nothing, under the Shepard tone. Measured: spectrum, cohesion and flow level (98.2 / 77.8 / 59.6); worth knowing - without the fall's clearer edge compscore's section count flipped 7 -> 5 between seeds on these changes (77.4 on seed 0, 96.7 on seed 11 for the same song), reported to chirp-eco; with it the song reads 6 sections on both seeds. Not heard by me (and the spiral is stereo: listen on headphones).

ROUND TYPE: section, w8 (3:37-4:07, bars 85-96, the drift's second half, the last look before the fall), flagged static. Rewritten after Harry's 6 Nov note (a hook you can hum; tone is home) as THE SEED, PLAINLY: E1 - the album's hook - sung the right way up, at its own speed, on an ondes Martenot (a near-sine voice gliding on its ribbon), nine times through its 5-beat cycle against the bar, so it lands somewhere new each time and comes home on bar 96 as the fall begins. v7 87.20 (seeds 0/11 87.20/87.04 vs v6 94.48 rescored now; KEPT on Harry's direction of 6 Nov 00:30 - tone is home, no stacked clashes, a hook, a score may dip). ROUND TYPE: section drawn, EXTENDED to a whole-track tonal pass (Harry: big changes wanted). What was still clashing in t2, found by counting pitch classes per part: (1) the progression - Dm11 voiced with E, F and G stacked, and Fmaj7#11 with a B against the F - is now consonant D Dorian in stacked thirds: Dm9 | Fmaj9 | Cadd9 | Am7; (2) the NES triangle bass moved E2's cell by TRANSPOSITION onto each chord root, which put E-flat, A-flat and B-flat in the bass 78 times; it now moves the cell DIATONICALLY (root, fifth, third, seventh of each chord in D Dorian): no chromatic bass note left; (3) the crest's stretto answered a fifth above the pulse (an F# against the F): it now answers on D, a fifth below; (4) the Kuramoto swarm's spread is 12 cents instead of 26, so free it is a chorus rather than a detuned cloud, and it still locks at the crest; (5) the ondes sings E1 at the crest too (bars 49-52, three times) where E1 first turns the right way up - the payoff is a tune, not only a chip pulse. Per-window levels are unchanged to 0.1 dB; the cost is in compscore's segmentation (variety 94 -> 80, recurrence 88 -> 65: consonant harmony gives weaker section boundaries). Tried: a tighter swarm (coupling floor 1.0) - same score; the old 26-cent spread with the new chords - 84.1. Not heard by me.
